correctness.rationale: The continuous-time embedding has exact feasible-edge selection probabilities proportional to pair-size products. Compensated martingale quadratic variations vanish at order 1/n on compact intervals, giving the three-dimensional fluid ODE. A direct exact polynomial identity verifies x=a(1-bu)(1-cu) and cyclic permutations with u prime=(1-au)(1-bu)(1-cu); u increases to 1/a. The terminal-time truncation is rigorous both for a>b (small parts asymptotically exhausted while the largest dominates) and for a=b (all populations vanish). Pair-type compensators integrate to b(1-c/(2a)), c(1-b/(2a)), bc/(2a). The exact graph maximum and two-case arithmetic-geometric-mean optimization give a unique sharp 7/8 lower efficiency ratio. The packaged no-dependency checker passed 3311 exact rational and symbolic assertions, with labeled-edge enumeration independent of aggregate-state recursion. Random diagnostics are not proof of limits.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: A result for two equal leading parts does not imply a formula for three strictly positive proportions and a unique extremizer at unequal leading sizes. value.rationale: Uniform edge-greedy matching is a canonical random sequential graph algorithm. Dense complete tripartite graphs isolate the nontrivial cost of small-part edges, with a precise positive-density loss bc/(2a), an exact triple of edge-type frequencies, and a complete sharp efficiency classification. The unique 2:1:1 worst-proportion witness K_{2n,n,n} has a perfect matching yet greedy selection loses asymptotically one eighth, making the constant a nontrivial algorithmic benchmark, not arbitrary finite data or an already-covered substitution.
